questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The Russell–Saunders ground-state term symbol for a free $\text{V}^{3+}$ ($3d^2$) ion is
questions.explanationEn: For $3d^2$, placing two parallel electrons in $m_l = +2$ and $+1$ gives $S = 1$ ($2S+1 = 3$) and $L = 2 + 1 = 3$ ($F$ term). Since the $d$-subshell is less than half-filled, the ground state has minimum $J = |L - S| = |3 - 1| = 2$, yielding $^3F_2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following mixed-metal oxides adopts a **normal** spinel structure, $[\text{A}]_{\text{tet}}[\text{B}_2]_{\text{oct}}\text{O}_4$?
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{Co}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{Co}^{2+}$ $d^7$ and $2\,\text{Co}^{3+}$ $d^6$), the $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ions are low-spin $d^6$ ($t_{2g}^6$) in the oxide octahedral field, possessing an exceptionally large octahedral site preference energy (OSPE). Thus all $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ions occupy octahedral sites and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ occupies tetrahedral sites: $[\text{Co}^{2+}]_{\text{tet}}[\text{Co}^{3+}_2]_{\text{oct}}\text{O}_4$ (normal spinel). $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, $\text{NiFe}_2\text{O}_4$, and $\text{CuFe}_2\text{O}_4$ are inverse spinels.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The IUPAC name of the coordination compound $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$ is
questions.explanationEn: The counter-cation $\text{K}^+$ is named simply as 'potassium' (no multiplicative prefix). Because the complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ is anionic, iron is named 'ferrate', and since oxalato is a bidentate ligand with three units, 'tris(oxalato)' is used. Oxidation state of $\text{Fe}$: $x + 3(-2) = -3 \implies x = +3$. Hence: potassium tris(oxalato)ferrate(III).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In ferrocene, $[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$, the hapticity of each cyclopentadienyl ring and the formal oxidation state of iron (using the ionic counting convention) are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In ferrocene, all five carbon atoms of each cyclopentadienyl ring bind equally to iron ($\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5$). Treating each $\text{Cp}^-$ ligand as a $6\pi$-electron aromatic monoanion assigns iron a formal oxidation state of $+2$ ($d^6$, total $6 + 6 + 6 = 18\text{ e}^-$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: During the complexometric titration of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with $\text{Na}_2\text{H}_2\text{EDTA}$ in an $\text{NH}_3/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ buffer at $\text{pH } 10$ using Eriochrome Black T (EBT) as indicator, the color change observed at the endpoint is from
questions.explanationEn: At $\text{pH } 10$, the free indicator $\text{HIn}^{2-}$ is sky-blue, while the $\text{Mg}-\text{In}^-$ complex is wine-red. At the endpoint, EDTA quantitatively displaces the indicator from $\text{Mg}-\text{In}^-$, changing the solution from wine-red to sky-blue.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The markedly higher thermodynamic stability of $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$ compared to $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ in aqueous solution (the **chelate effect**) is primarily driven by
optionsEn: a large negative enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ \ll 0$) because $\text{Ni}-\text{N}$ bonds in $\text{en}$ are much stronger than in $\text{NH}_3$

a large positive entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ > 0$) because replacing six monodentate $\text{NH}_3$ ligands with three bidentate $\text{en}$ ligands produces a net increase in the number of independent particles in solution
a large increase in $\Delta_o$ making $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$ diamagnetic
questions.explanationEn: For $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} + 3\,\text{en} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+} + 6\,\text{NH}_3$, the $\text{Ni}-\text{N}$ bond strengths are very similar ($\Delta H^\circ$ is small), but $4$ reactant particles yield $7$ product particles ($\Delta n = +3$), producing a large positive $\Delta S^\circ$ and strongly negative $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When Vaska's complex, $\textit{trans}\text{-[IrCl(CO)(PPh}_3)_2]$ ($\nu_{\text{CO}} = 1967\text{ cm}^{-1}$), undergoes oxidative addition with $\text{H}_2$ to form $[\text{Ir(H)}_2\text{Cl(CO)(PPh}_3)_2]$, the formal oxidation state of $\text{Ir}$, total valence electron count, and $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ change as follows:
questions.explanationEn: Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ oxidizes $\text{Ir(I)}$ ($16\text{ e}^-$) to $\text{Ir(III)}$ ($18\text{ e}^-$). The higher oxidation state makes $\text{Ir(III)}$ less electron-rich, reducing $\text{Ir} \to \text{CO}$ $\pi$-back-bonding and causing $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ to increase (from $1967\text{ cm}^{-1}$ to $\sim 2070\text{ cm}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the redox titration of oxalic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$) with standardized $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium at $\sim 60\,^\circ\text{C}$, the solution is acidified with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ rather than $\text{HCl}$ because
optionsEn: $\text{HCl}$ is too weak an acid to protonate $\text{MnO}_4^-$
$\text{MnO}_4^-$ oxidizes $\text{Cl}^-$ ions from $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{Cl}_2$ gas, causing a positive titration error
questions.explanationEn: Because $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}) = +1.51\text{ V} > E^\circ(\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-) = +1.36\text{ V}$, permanganate oxidizes $\text{Cl}^-$ to $\text{Cl}_2$ (especially when catalyzed by $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ or heated), consuming extra titrant. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is non-oxidizable and non-reducing.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the solid state, $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ and $\text{Co}_2(\text{CO})_8$ both obey the $18$-electron rule per metal center. The number of **bridging** $\text{CO}$ ligands ($\mu_2\text{-CO}$) in solid $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ and solid $\text{Co}_2(\text{CO})_8$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Solid $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ ($D_{4d}$) has **zero** bridging carbonyls — two staggered $\text{Mn(CO)}_5$ units joined solely by an unsupported $\text{Mn}-\text{Mn}$ single bond. Solid $\text{Co}_2(\text{CO})_8$ ($C_{2v}$) has **two** $\mu_2\text{-CO}$ bridging ligands, six terminal $\text{CO}$ ligands, and one $\text{Co}-\text{Co}$ single bond.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an octahedral $d^6$ transition metal complex, the crystal field stabilization energies (including pairing energy $P$) for the high-spin and low-spin states, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: In a free $d^6$ ion (Hund's rule), there is already $1$ electron pair. In high-spin $O_h$ ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$), there is still $1$ pair ($0$ extra pairings) and $\text{CFSE} = 4(-0.4) + 2(+0.6) = -0.4\Delta_o$. In low-spin $O_h$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$), there are $3$ pairs ($2$ extra pairings beyond the free ion), so $\text{CFSE} = 6(-0.4)\Delta_o + 2P = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding electronic absorption spectra of transition metal complexes is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The Laporte selection rule forbids $g \to g$ and $u \to u$ transitions in centrosymmetric molecules.

Octahedral $d\text{--}d$ transitions gain weak intensity ($\varepsilon \approx 5\text{--}50\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) through vibronic coupling (asymmetric vibrations temporarily breaking the inversion center).
Spin-forbidden transitions ($\Delta S \neq 0$) gain very weak intensity ($\varepsilon \approx 0.01\text{--}1\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) via spin–orbit coupling.
Charge-transfer transitions are Laporte-forbidden and therefore weaker than $d\text{--}d$ transitions.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all textbook spectroscopic selection-rule mechanisms.
- (D) False: Charge-transfer transitions (LMCT and MLCT) are typically both spin-allowed and Laporte-allowed, making them $100\text{--}1000$ times *more* intense ($\varepsilon \sim 10^3\text{--}10^5$) than $d\text{--}d$ bands.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following organometallic complexes obey(s) the **$18$-electron rule**?
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) $[\text{Cr(CO)}_6]$: $6 + 6(2) = 18\text{ e}^-$. True.
- (B) $[\text{Mn(CO)}_5]^-$: $7 + 1 + 5(2) = 18\text{ e}^-$. True.
- (C) $[\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-Cp})(\text{CO})_2\text{Cl}]$: $8 + 5 + 2(2) + 1 = 18\text{ e}^-$. True.
- (D) $[\text{Co}(\eta^5\text{-Cp})_2]$: $9 + 2(5) = 19\text{ e}^-$ (does not obey $18\text{ e}^-$ rule). False.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about hemoglobin ($\text{Hb}$) and myoglobin ($\text{Mb}$) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: In deoxy-myoglobin, $\text{Fe(II)}$ is $5$-coordinate (square pyramidal), high-spin ($S = 2$), and lies roughly $0.4\text{ \AA}$ out of the porphyrin plane toward the proximal histidine.
Upon binding $\text{O}_2$, the iron center in oxy-myoglobin becomes $6$-coordinate, diamagnetic, and moves into the plane of the porphyrin ring.
Myoglobin has a higher $\text{O}_2$ affinity (lower $P_{50}$) than hemoglobin, enabling efficient oxygen transfer from blood to muscle tissue.
Both hemoglobin and myoglobin are tetrameric proteins.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Hemoglobin is a tetramer ($\alpha_2\beta_2$), whereas myoglobin is a **monomer** containing a single polypeptide chain and one heme unit.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding chlorophyll and coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The macrocycle in vitamin/coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ is a **corrin** ring, which lacks one methine bridge compared to a porphyrin ring (having a direct $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond between rings A and D).
Chlorophyll contains a long hydrophobic **phytol** ester tail that anchors it into the thylakoid membrane/protein complex.
In vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ (cyanocobalamin), the upper axial ligand is $-\text{CN}$, whereas in coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ it is a $5'$-deoxyadenosyl group.
Both chlorophyll and coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ contain $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ as their central metal ion.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Chlorophyll contains $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ contains $\text{Co}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total valence electron count of iron in ferrocene, $[\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$, is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Using the neutral-ligand method: $\text{Fe}$ (Group 8) $= 8\text{ e}^-$ and two $\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5$ radicals $= 2 \times 5 = 10\text{ e}^-$, giving $8 + 10 = 18$ valence electrons.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of microstates possible for a free $\text{V}^{3+}$ ($3d^2$) ion is _______.
questions.explanationEn: A $d$-subshell has $2(2l+1) = 10$ spin-orbitals. For $2$ electrons, $W = \binom{10}{2} = \frac{10 \times 9}{2} = 45$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In sodium nitroprusside, $\text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5(\text{NO})]$, the nitrosyl ligand is linear ($\text{NO}^+$). The formal oxidation state of iron in this complex is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
In the complex anion $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5(\text{NO})]^{2-}$, treating $\text{CN}^-$ as $-1$ and linear $\text{NO}$ as $\text{NO}^+$ ($+1$):
$x + 5(-1) + (+1) = -2 \implies x - 4 = -2 \implies x = +2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of significant figures in the measured quantity $0.0045020\text{ g}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Leading zeros ($0.00$) are placeholders and not significant. The non-zero digits ($4, 5, 2$), the captive zero ($0$ between $5$ and $2$), and the trailing zero after the decimal point ($0$) are all significant, giving $5$ significant figures.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The spin-only magnetic moment of octahedral $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ is _______ $\mu_B$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8$) in an octahedral field has configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$, with $n = 2$ unpaired electrons.
$\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\mu_B = \sqrt{2 \times 4}\,\mu_B = \sqrt{8}\,\mu_B \approx 2.83\,\mu_B$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of microstates for a free $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^3$) ion is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
For $3$ electrons in $10$ $d$-spin-orbitals:
$W = \binom{10}{3} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 120$.
